content.comment_body: This is my first post and I'm writing it using a text editor on Linux. I noticed that tabs added for formatting are removed upon pasting into the [company_name] forum. Is there a way to preserve these tabs? It would make the formatted text more readable. I am working with two [product_name] modules and would like to transfer data between them using network outputs and inputs. My goal is to set up the configuration manually, without utilizing any project wizard. I've created a mock-up where a network output (NQ) on one device triggers a network input (NI) on the other device, but it isn't functioning as intended. Here's the process I follow: - Assign IP addresses - Establish Ethernet connections - Configure NQ1 and NI1 For IP assignment: Device1: IP 192.168.1.7, program test-1-007-server.lsc Device2: IP 192.168.1.8, program test-1-008-client.lsc To set up the Ethernet connection, I use the diagram tools to add and configure server connections with TSAP settings. NQ1 is configured to send its value to a remote device at IP 192.168.1.8, TSAP 20.00, with the corresponding block type and number. NI1 is similarly configured to receive from 192.168.1.7, TSAP 20.00 or 21.00, as both may be tested. After simulation, neither configuration achieves data transfer between the modules. Adjusting TSAP values doesn't resolve the issue. My main questions: 1) Why are client connections created automatically and why can't they be edited? 2) Why does the device at 192.168.1.7 need a client connection, while in network projects the server TSAP typically transmits data? 3) What is preventing the setup from working? 4) What is the correct manual approach? 5) Is it possible to add client connections directly via the tools instead of letting automatic configurations take over? Thanks in advance. Attached are both configuration files.

Hello, I replicated your configuration using the network project feature in the [product_name] software and confirmed that it should work, though I didn’t check the IP settings directly. For best results, set up both modules as part of the same network project from the beginning rather than as separate devices. Splitting the editor into two screens can help manage the process more smoothly. You can also find helpful examples for download on the official support site.
Hello, Please upload your program so the community can review it.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are struggling to manually configure network connections between two [product_name] controllers, without using the network wizard provided by the [company_name] software. The main issues include automatic creation of client connections that are locked from editing, unclear feedback about why data isn’t transferring, and confusion surrounding TSAP assignments and overall connection logic.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to independently set up working network communication between two [product_name] controllers using specified IP and TSAP parameters as well as block configurations. They expect to have clear control over connection creation and visibility, along with straightforward software feedback and the ability to adjust all settings manually.
